blocks.h2: Water Treatment Options for McHenry County Homes

tiles.body: Remove the hardness minerals that leave scale in water heaters, fixtures and pipes.
Take out the iron that stains sinks, tubs and laundry orange.
Catch sand and particles before they reach fixtures and appliances.
Under-sink reverse osmosis for cooking and drinking water.

bodies: McHenry County gets its water from shallow and deep aquifers, so what comes out of the tap depends on which wells feed your home. Groundwater here tends to be hard, and some areas carry iron or manganese. A water test tells you exactly what's in yours.

If you're on a private well, testing matters even more. Health officials recommend testing private wells regularly, because no utility is doing it for you. We test for hardness, iron and other common issues and use the results to recommend only what your home needs.

blocks.intro: Water is one of the biggest plumbing stories in McHenry County.

items.body: Groundwater tends to be hard across the county. It leaves scale on fixtures, sediment in water heaters and a film on glass shower doors.

Orange or rust-colored stains in sinks, tubs and toilets usually come from iron. Outside city limits, unincorporated Eastwood Manor, on a small private water system, lived with iron-heavy water for years until a filtration upgrade in 2025.
Many homes outside city limits in McHenry County are on private wells. Testing is the owner's job, and a filter or softener is often part of the setup.
A softener that's out of salt, set wrong or not regenerating lets hardness right through. We service and adjust them.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Why are there orange stains in my sinks and tub?
items.answer: Orange or rust-colored stains usually come from iron in the water. It isn't a health hazard, but it stains fixtures and laundry and settles in your water heater. An iron filter takes it out.

items.q: Do I need a water softener in McHenry?
items.preview: Most homes on hard groundwater benefit. A test confirms it.
items.answer: Most homes on hard groundwater see a real difference: less scale, longer water heater life and fewer spots. A test shows how hard your water is so you can decide.

items.q: How often should I test my private well?
items.preview: Regularly. Health officials suggest at least once a year for bacteria.
items.answer: Health officials generally recommend testing a private well at least once a year for bacteria, and after any flooding or changes in taste, color or smell. We can test for hardness and iron at the same time.

items.q: My softener has salt but the water still feels hard. Why?
items.preview: It may not be regenerating, or the settings are wrong.
items.answer: The softener may not be regenerating, the resin may be worn out or the hardness setting may be too low for your water. We can test and adjust it.

items.q: How much does a water softener or filter cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the system and your water. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the type and size of the system and how it connects to your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
